speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of a thickened endometrial stripe and an adnexal mass are concerning for ovarian cancer with endometrial involvement. I will now request a CA-125 blood test and a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to further characterize the mass and check for metastasis. REQUEST TEST: CA-125, CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CA-125 is normal, we must rule out other causes like endometrial hyperplasia or a benign ovarian cyst. I will now request an endometrial biopsy to evaluate the thickened lining. REQUEST TEST: Endometrial Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Endometrial Biopsy shows Well-differentiated adenocarcinoma

speaker: Doctor
text: The endometrial biopsy confirms well-differentiated adenocarcinoma, indicating endometrial cancer is the primary issue. The adnexal mass may represent metastatic disease or a separate benign process, but the endometrial cancer requires immediate staging and treatment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial Adenocarcinoma
